correctness.rationale: For Cr_n=K_{n,n} minus a perfect matching, the complement I of a double outer-independent dominating set is independent. It is either contained in one bipartition side or exactly the unmatched pair {a_i,b_i}. In a one-sided complement case the selected opposite side is complete, and at least two vertices must also be selected on the first side (one cannot defend its unmatched b_i); every choice of two suffices. Thus |D|≥n+2, and there are 2*C(n,2) such equality sets. A two-sided independent complement yields |D|=2n−2 and is feasible for n≥3. Comparing gives γ_d^{oi}=min(n+2,2n−2)=n+2 for n≥4; n=4 has four additional optimum unmatched-pair complements (total 16), n≥5 has precisely n(n−1). A separately written direct all-subsets checker verifies the complete minimizer set for n=4,5,6. This finite check is corroboration, not the all-n argument.
residual_risks: The n=3 boundary is C6, whose scalar domination number is already covered elsewhere; theorem starts n≥4.

value.rationale: A crown graph is a standard highly symmetric perfect-matching deletion from a complete bipartite graph. The theorem resolves the exact increase of the double outer-independent domination number and gives every optimal set, with a genuinely distinct equality geometry at n=4. This is a natural infinite-family equality classification, beyond an edge-removal bound.
residual_risks: The formula concerns matched balanced complete bipartite deletions, not arbitrary matching-deleted K_{p,q}.

limitations: The n=3 scalar is previously implied by the known C6 formula.
